description: How mobile networks are built and run end to end: cellular concepts and spectrum, the GSM, UMTS, LTE and 5G architectures and their protocols, mobility management and roaming, and the SMS, USSD and data services that carry mobile money and everyday traffic. Every procedure, from attach and handover to a USSD session, is traced message by message in a network simulator, and a network is planned for real coverage and traffic targets.
modelledOn: 3GPP Technical Specifications for GSM, UMTS, LTE and 5G NR
Sauter, From GSM to LTE-Advanced Pro and 5G: An Introduction to Mobile Networks and Mobile Broadband
Holma and Toskala, LTE for UMTS: Evolution to LTE-Advanced
Dahlman, Parkvall and Skold, 5G NR: The Next Generation Wireless Access Technology
outcomes: Explain the cellular concept and plan cells, frequency reuse and capacity for a given coverage area and traffic load.
Describe the radio access and core networks of GSM, UMTS, LTE and 5G and the role of each network element and interface.
Trace signalling procedures such as attach, authentication, bearer setup, paging and handover across the protocol stack.
Analyse mobility management, location updating and roaming and their cost in signalling load and latency.
Design SMS, USSD and mobile data services and explain how the operator's network delivers and charges for them.
Compare 4G and 5G deployment options and assess them for urban and rural coverage in Ghana and the wider region.

units.title: Cellular concepts and the evolution of mobile networks
topics: Generations of mobile networks from 1G analogue to 5G: what each added in services, data rate and architecture; the roles of 3GPP and the ITU
Cells, clusters and frequency reuse; reuse distance, co-channel interference and the signal-to-interference ratio
Capacity: cell splitting, sectoring, microcells, picocells and small cells; traffic in Erlangs and grade of service
Macro, micro and umbrella cell layers; coverage-limited versus capacity-limited cells
Mobile markets in Africa: operator landscape, tower sharing, mobile penetration and the rural coverage gap

units.title: Radio access and spectrum
topics: Spectrum bands for 2G to 5G (sub-1 GHz, mid-band, millimetre wave); the coverage and capacity trade-offs of each
Spectrum licensing and auctions; the National Communications Authority and spectrum policy in Ghana
Duplexing (FDD, TDD) and multiple access (FDMA, TDMA, CDMA, OFDMA) as used by each generation
Link budget and cell range; why low bands matter for rural cell coverage
Base station hardware: antennas, remote radio heads, baseband units; backhaul over microwave, fibre and satellite

units.title: GSM architecture and protocols
topics: GSM network elements: MS, SIM, BTS, BSC, MSC, HLR, VLR, AuC, EIR; the Um, Abis and A interfaces
Air interface: TDMA frames, timeslots, logical channels (traffic, broadcast, common and dedicated control)
Signalling: SS7, MAP and the GSM protocol stack (LAPDm, RR, MM, CM)
Call setup for mobile-originated and mobile-terminated calls; paging and channel assignment
Security: IMSI and TMSI, A3 and A8 challenge-response authentication, A5 ciphering and the known weaknesses of 2G

units.title: GPRS and 3G UMTS
topics: GPRS and EDGE: packet data over GSM, SGSN and GGSN, PDP contexts, the Gn and Gi interfaces
UMTS architecture: UTRAN with NodeB and RNC, the Iub and Iu interfaces, circuit-switched and packet-switched domains
WCDMA radio: spreading, fast power control, soft handover and the near-far problem
HSPA and HSPA+: higher data rates, fast scheduling and the shift to data-dominated traffic
Mutual authentication with AKA and the improvements over GSM security

units.title: 4G LTE: E-UTRAN and the Evolved Packet Core
topics: Flat all-IP architecture: eNodeB, MME, S-GW, P-GW, HSS, PCRF; the S1, X2 and S11 interfaces
LTE radio: OFDMA downlink, SC-FDMA uplink, resource blocks, frame structure, MIMO and carrier aggregation
Protocol stack: PDCP, RLC, MAC and PHY in the user plane; RRC and NAS in the control plane
Attach, default and dedicated bearers, QoS class identifiers and policy control
Voice over LTE with IMS; circuit-switched fallback as a transition
Simulating an LTE attach and measuring control-plane latency

units.title: Mobility management and roaming
topics: Idle-mode mobility: location, routing and tracking areas; the trade-off between location updating and paging
Connected-mode handover: measurement reports, hard, soft and X2-based handover, inter-RAT handover
Handover failures, ping-pong and parameter tuning (hysteresis, time to trigger)
National and international roaming: home routing versus local breakout, HLR and VLR signalling, GRX and IPX
Cross-border roaming arrangements in East and West Africa and their effect on what subscribers pay

units.title: 5G networks
topics: 5G use cases: enhanced mobile broadband, massive machine-type communication, ultra-reliable low-latency communication
5G NR radio: flexible numerology, bandwidth parts, massive MIMO and beamforming, millimetre wave
5G core service-based architecture: AMF, SMF, UPF, AUSF, UDM, PCF, NRF; HTTP-based service interfaces
Non-standalone and standalone deployment options; dual connectivity with LTE
Network slicing, multi-access edge computing and the virtualised, cloud-native core
Fixed wireless access and the business case for 5G in African cities versus extending 4G to rural areas

units.title: Mobile data services, SMS and USSD
topics: SMS: the SMSC, store and forward, MAP signalling, delivery reports, SMS over IMS and bulk SMS gateways
USSD: session-oriented signalling, mobile-initiated and network-initiated sessions, the USSD gateway and session timeouts
Designing USSD menus for mobile money and government services: shortcodes such as *170#, menu depth and session limits
Mobile data services: APNs, DNS, carrier-grade NAT, data bundles and charging (online and offline charging, the OCS)
Security and fraud in mobile services: SIM swap, SS7 attacks, SMS one-time passwords and their weaknesses

units.title: Network planning, operations and capstone
topics: Radio network planning: coverage prediction, capacity dimensioning, site selection and drive tests
Key performance indicators: call setup success, drop rate, handover success, throughput; network optimisation
Network management with OSS and BSS; powering off-grid sites with solar and generators
Capstone: plan an LTE network for a rural Ghanaian district and simulate attach, handover and a USSD transaction across it
